feed.title: callgraph releases
feed.subtitle: What was added, changed and fixed in each callgraph release.

entry.title: callgraph v1.1.1
entry.content:
Added

  • A short impact view with --compact: --grep … --depth N --compact prints the callers level by level, one line per file (path: A() L12, B() L40 ← target, wrapped at about 160 characters), so a wide impact analysis stays short. Route registrations show their actual code, for example L5 Route::delete('songs', [SongController::class, 'destroy'])->name('songs.destroy'). When all entries of a file point to the same target, ← target is printed once, right after the file name. Over MCP it is the find_callers parameter compact: true.
  • locate understands a plain sentence: write the task as you would say it. Common English and Hungarian filler words (hol, a, az, hogy, …) are ignored and listed as ignored: … in the header; quoted phrases are still searched as phrases. Matches in translation files (Laravel lang files, JSON/TS dictionaries, .po / .xliff) count much less, so a code file whose name or symbol matches ranks above them. When most words match only UI text, the header suggests adding the English code name; when nothing matches in code, it says so (no code match) and keeps the list, which helps if you are looking for a UI label.

Changed

  • --grep / find_callers finds exactly the name you give: execute no longer matches executeCommand, and store (a method) no longer matches the class Store. A class name still finds its qualified calls (SongService matches App\Services\SongService::x). For the old "contains" search use a regex, for example '.*execute.*'; regex and Type::method patterns stay case-insensitive.
  • Cleaner call lists for Go and Rust: in Go outlines a call on the method's own object shows as a plain method name (like PHP $this->x), and other calls as Type::method. In Rust, a call through nested fields (self.a.b.m()) is no longer listed as a certain caller in --depth; it appears only with --guess.
  • update / callgraph.sh update [--dev] reminds you to reconnect MCP: after a successful update it prints a note that a running MCP server keeps the old version until you reconnect it (Claude Code: /mcp, then Reconnect).

Fixed

  • --grep Type::method and --depth N find callers that were missed: Python calls through self. / cls. and Go calls on the method's own object, typed parameters, typed local variables (also multi-value assignments) and method chains. Before, the result could say that nothing calls the method, or the level-2 list in Python could come back empty.
  • --depth lists every route to an action: a routes file with several [Controller::class, 'method'] routes showed only the first at level 2, and two routes to the same action showed only one; now each is listed. --grep 'Ctrl::m' --depth N on the controller action itself lists its route registrations at level 1; before, it said there were no callers. When a short Ctrl::method pattern matches same-named classes in several namespaces, each level-1 route row names its fully-qualified target, in the normal and --compact views.

entry.title: callgraph v1.1.0
entry.content:
Added

  • Blade templates (.blade.php) are analysed as their own language (before, the result was empty): one view per file, named like admin.users.index, with sections, pushes and slots as line ranges; @extends / @include / @each / <x-…> / <livewire:…> resolve to the view files, so the callers of a layout list the views extending it; @props show as properties; PHP inside {{ }}, {!! !!}, @php and directive arguments is analysed; @if / @foreach … appear as control flow; route('x') links to the Laravel route (→ POST /users · Controller@method, unknown names are flagged); __() / @lang take part in the i18n check; and a "rendered by" line lists the view('…') calls in controllers.
  • MCP undo tool: restores the last change made by generate or rename — one file when a file is given, otherwise the whole last group of changes. The history is multi-step: each call steps one change further back (before, two undos in a row toggled the last change). Like generate and rename, it only exists when the server runs with --generate / CALLGRAPH_GENERATE=1, and it is marked readOnlyHint: false.
  • rename term <old> <new>: rename a whole concept in every spelling: rename term post article changes the word in PHP, JS, TS and Vue code wherever it appears as a whole word, keeping the case and plural: Post / post / posts, post_id, StorePostRequest, /posts/{post}, admin.posts.index, Posts/Index.vue. Plurals with -s, -es and -ies are formed automatically; an irregular one is given as person/people. Files whose path contains the word are moved, and if the migrations create tables (also pivot tables) or *_id columns with the word, a new reversible migration renames them (rename_post_to_article); existing migrations are not touched. Skipped: all-caps words (POST), HTTP-verb calls (->post(, Route::post(, postJson(), vendor and node_modules. A quoted word in value position that may be an HTTP verb ('method' => 'post') is only flagged, not changed. --dry shows the whole plan (files moved, changes per file, flagged strings, the migration), and one undo reverts everything, including the new migration. Over MCP it is the term kind of the rename tool.
  • gen previews and more placement options: with --into / --replace, --dry first prints where the code would go, e.g. → app/Pay.php::Pay after charge (L41) or → f.vue: script L12-14, and --diff shows a --replace as a short unified diff without writing anything. For PHP --into, --before <method> and --at L<n> place the code before a method or at a line (an --at outside the class body, e.g. on the { line, is rejected upfront with the body's line range), and --upsert turns an --into of an existing method into a replace (with --expect, the expectation is checked when the member already exists). Vue --into file.vue::template#id (or ::#id, ::.class) appends inside that template element, the expression being read as template markup, and --replace file.vue::script / ::template / ::style replaces the whole content of that section (the tags stay), with no line range that can go stale. The MCP generate tool got before, at, upsert and diff.
  • gen PHP: traits, anonymous classes and Laravel class names: use:HasFactory,Notifiable under a type writes use HasFactory, Notifiable; inside the class body (c:Post<Model> > use:HasFactory + +comments():HasMany{…}). a:<Migration> > +up():void{…} writes an anonymous class, return new class extends Migration { … };, as in Laravel migrations. In a Laravel project (laravel/framework in composer.json) common framework classes such as Model, Schema, Blueprint, Route, Request, Rule, Builder, HasMany or RefreshDatabase are imported without use:; names that exist in several packages (e.g. Response) still need use:.
  • gen PHP statements outside a class: php{ … } and raw{ … }: php{ Route::get('/posts', [PostController::class, 'index']); } writes plain PHP code. With --write routes/x.php it creates the file (adding <?php and the imports), with --into routes/web.php it appends to the end of the file or goes to --at L<n> / --after L<n>, and with --replace bootstrap/app.php:L14-L16 it replaces that line range or a method. The code takes the indentation of the line it goes at or replaces, and an empty php{} with --replace file:La-Lb deletes the lines. raw{ … } writes the text exactly as given, e.g. a Blade view with --write resources/views/app.blade.php; Blade files are not PHP-syntax-checked.
  • Vue props from interfaces, defaults and defineModel: defineProps<Props>() now resolves a local interface or type alias (including extends and A & B); withDefaults defaults are shown as type $name = default and the prop is not marked required; defineModel appears as model: in the outline and as a model section in --format api. A type-only defineEmits now shows its real line.
  • Kotlin support (.kt, .kts): classes, data/sealed/enum classes, objects and companion objects, interfaces, top-level and extension functions, suspend and @Composable functions, properties (including by lazy and by viewModels()), calls with receiver type resolution, ::ref / Type::name references and control flow. Categories cover Compose (views, modifiers, API), coroutines, Android and the Kotlin standard library; *.gradle.kts files are marked as Gradle build scripts. hiltViewModel(), viewModel() and by viewModels() are injection edges, and calls on the view model resolve to its type. Hilt @Inject constructor, @Provides and @Binds show what is injected and which method provides a type. NavHost composable("route") { Screen() } and navController.navigate("…") are navigation edges (type-safe routes too, navigate(Detail(…)) / composable<Detail>), also when the NavHost is in another file. Callers of an interface method and of its implementations see each other. Android projects get a profile (ui / view model / data / domain / di layers; *.gradle.kts is not counted as app code), and Kotlin appears in the usage statistics. !! does not hide the receiver of a call, *Test.kt files and androidTest folders count as tests in locate, and method bodies are filtered correctly (comments, raw strings).
  • Swift callbacks, protocols and navigation: a method reference passed as a callback argument (Composer(onSend: vm.send)) is a call of that method. A closure stored in a callback property (socket.onFrame = { … }) is linked to where the property is invoked. Callers of a protocol method and of its implementations see each other (via), and a conformance declared in an extension counts. .environment(store) / .environmentObject are injection edges, and views built in navigationDestination, sheet, fullScreenCover, popover or NavigationLink are navigation edges. Receiver types are taken from @State, @Bindable, let x: T, @Environment(T.self) and parameters. A reference passed positionally (.onChange(of: x, vm.changed)) or via #selector(…) is a reference call; key paths are not calls. SwiftData @Query var items: [Item] is a model edge and modelContext calls are categorized. Each view in a navigationDestination { switch … } is a navigation edge, generic views (List<Item>(…)) count as component uses, and actor methods resolve. A call through a property chain that spans files (self.store.session.user.load()) resolves to the method of the last property's type. The method that invokes a stored closure (onFrame?(…)) is listed as a direct caller of the closure's callees, as via <Type>::<property>; these callers and callers resolved across files (Kotlin routes, Swift property chains, Rust trait bounds) are shown at the first level of the callers list, under "called through a stored closure or resolved across files".
  • callgraph mcp --allow <dir>: lets the MCP server read an extra folder, e.g. a sibling ../android. Repeat the flag or set CALLGRAPH_MCP_ALLOW; by default the server stays restricted to the project root.
  • Rust: function references and more receiver types: a function or method passed as a value (.map(Self::parse), .and_then(Foo::new), .map(helper)) is a call. Receivers typed by a generic bound (T: Trait, where) or by a method's return type (self.make()?, Type::open().unwrap()) are resolved. Loop variables (for b in self.bars), if let Some(x) / while let / match Some(x) bindings and iterator-closure parameters (items.iter().map(|x| x.name())) get their element type, so their method calls resolve; with T: A + B the trait that declares the method is used, also when the traits are declared in other files. #[test] / #[tokio::test] functions and #[cfg(test)] modules are marked as tests, Some / Ok / Err / Box::new / Default::default no longer clutter the call list, and calls of a local closure are marked dynamic. Callers of a trait method and of its implementations see each other in both directions (via).
  • JS/TS: functions passed as values are callers: a function handed over as a call or new argument, an array element or an object property value (also shorthand), e.g. the handler in a route table guarded(api.listX), is a reference edge marked (ref). It shows in callers lists, counts for --depth / impact, and the function no longer looks like it has no callers. This covers functions of the same file, local imports, object-literal methods and members of a namespace import (import * as api); package functions are not counted.
  • More JS/TS imports resolve to files: tsconfig extends (a string or an array, also chained) and references are followed, a paths entry may have several targets and a * in the middle (the longest matching prefix wins), and resolve.alias in vite.config.* / vitest.config.* is read (an object or [{find, replacement}], with fileURLToPath(new URL(…)) or path.resolve(__dirname, …)). An alias is used only if its target exists. So imports like @shared/api or @kit/… find their callers and deps no longer reports them as missing packages. Imports without an extension also find .tsx, .jsx, .mts, .cjs, .cts files and index.vue / index.tsx / index.jsx / index.mjs, and ./a.js in a TypeScript project resolves to a.ts. Import resolution is faster too: each folder is listed once instead of checking every candidate file.
  • PHP: X::class references: X::class, a callable pair [X::class, 'method'] (X::method) and an invokable controller in Route::get($uri, X::class) (X::__invoke) are reference edges marked (ref), resolved through use and the namespace. --grep X, locate X and --depth now also find the routes, config entries and bindings that name the class.
  • PHP: calls resolve through docblock types: a variable or property typed only in a docblock now leads to the right method, so its callers are found (before, --grep 'Model::method' could find no callers there). Read: @mixin on a class (Laravel API resources: $this->m() that the resource does not define goes to the model's m, except the resource's own helpers), @var above an assignment or a foreach (also element types such as Collection<Post> or Post[]), @property / @property-read, @param of an untyped parameter, @return and @method. Native type declarations win, and only a single unambiguous class is used (?Post / Post|null count).
  • Full Laravel route table with --format routes: on a Laravel project every route is one row with its method, full URI, action, name=, [middleware] and file:line, with the prefix, name and middleware of groups inherited through nesting. The same table feeds --format ziggy, inertia and forms. Routes generated in a loop from a literal config array (foreach (config('catalogue.pages') as $name => $page) Route::get($page['uri'], …)->name($name)) are expanded into real rows and are no longer dynamic: ziggy knows their names, and inertia knows their pages (a page component named in the config that does not exist is flagged). The stored route data is rebuilt once, quietly.
  • Laravel wiring the framework makes: calls that only exist through Laravel now link to their target, so the callers of the target list them: an Eloquent local scope call (Product::query()->stocked(), Product::stocked()) goes to scopeStocked; an event dispatch (E::dispatch(…), event(new E)) to its listener (found by handle(E $e), Event::listen or the $listen array); Job::dispatch(…) to the job's handle; ->notify(new N) to N::toMail; and Model::observe(O::class) / #[ObservedBy] to the observer's methods.
  • --format inertia flags props that are never passed: a page that declares a required prop which no render site and no HandleInertiaRequests::share key provides gets a ! never passed: x line. The stored graph is rebuilt once, quietly.
  • PHP config and lang files outline as key paths: a config/*.php or lang/*/*.php file that returns an array shows its keys as paths with their line numbers (pages.home.uri = '/').
  • Rust CLI and library profile: a crate with main.rs, lib.rs or bin targets gets a profile with its entry points, src/<module> folders as module layers, and workspace members listed. tests, benches, examples and fixture or golden-sample folders no longer make the project look like a web, Vue or SwiftUI project.
  • TypeScript interface members as properties: the members of an interface are listed as properties, optional ones with ?.
  • Broken links in Markdown and HTML are marked: a relative link to a missing file, or a #anchor with no matching heading, shows ⚠ missing.
  • Locked versions in package.json / composer.json: the outline shows the locked version next to each dependency key.
  • Translation keys with --format i18n: for a lang file it shows which keys are missing in the other locales and which are unused; for a key (lang/en.json::board.title) where it is used and its value per locale; for source code which used keys do not exist (⚠ missing in hu.json). Covers lang JSON and PHP files and $t / t / trans / __ / @lang / Lang::get usages. Dynamic keys (` x.${y} , concatenation) are never reported missing, and sentence-style keys (Laravel's "strings as keys") are never reported unused. TS / JS dictionary modules (export default { … } in locales/en.ts, i18n/de.ts) are language files too: missing, unused and unknown keys are reported for them, and their outline shows the key tree. With a project's own t() wrapper (a local module over vue-i18n or i18next that exports t), t('a.b') calls in scripts count as key uses. Keys are shown whole, with a shared prefix written once (a.b.{c, d}`), and the view is fast in projects without translation files.
  • Stylesheet class usage with --format classes: shows which templates and components use a class, and a lenient list of unused classes (dynamic class building and Tailwind utilities are never reported). Lang files, stylesheets and $t(…) calls also get a short hint in the outline, and the MCP framework_view tool got i18n and classes.
  • MCP guide tool with a topic: the optional topic parameter (e.g. {topic: "php"}) returns one detail file of the skill instead of the core manual, so clients that only use MCP can read them too. Topics: php, blade, js, jsx, vue, css, rust, swift, kotlin, python, go, gen, mcp, reference.

Changed

  • JS/TS/Vue file keys are relative to the project root: the file part of a key (ui/src/x.ts::fn) is relative to the nearest folder with .git or .callgraph (without one, the topmost folder of the package / workspace), with / on every platform. In a monorepo a file has one key, so --grep 'ui/src/x.ts::fn' finds its callers in every package; before, each importing package saw its own relative key. Single-package projects keep their keys. The stored graph is rebuilt once, quietly.
  • Shorter skill, details per language: the agent skill is now a much shorter English core SKILL.md plus detail files in ref/ (php, blade, js, jsx, vue, css, rust, swift, kotlin, python, go, gen, mcp, reference) that the agent reads only for the languages of the project. Kotlin, Blade and React (ref/jsx.md: components, hooks, current limits) are covered in the skill for the first time. self-update installs the new layout.
  • Less noise in the framework views: --format events, middleware, validation, jobs, providers and di match their patterns only at the right place, so e.g. config or response no longer show up as events, while X::dispatch and Event::listen are listed. The middleware label is no longer glued to its target, and validation only counts strings that are real rule lists. References are not calls in these views, so belongsTo(Event::class) is not listed as an event dispatch.
  • Laravel views show the wiring: --format events lists wired lines (dispatch site → listener) and observer lines; jobs lists the queued classes (ShouldQueue) and wired lines for jobs and notifications, and no longer lists event dispatches; middleware shows which routes use each middleware; providers counts registration calls only inside service provider classes, so a model's boot or a query's bind (e.g. in tests) is not listed.
  • Cleaner rows in the outline and views: enum and constant reads in PHP show as const_use instead of external_call; --format routes rows no longer end in @ __top__::__top__, and Vue method index rows no longer carry [private].
  • Single-file output uses a relative path: when a show output contains the project path only once, the FILE path is relative and there is no root: line, so it can be copied into the next call.
  • Stories count as tests: story files (*.story.*, *.stories.*) and stories / storybook folders are tests in the project profile, not pages.
  • The Laravel form check follows form.transform(...): --format forms, the form: lines and the form ↔ rules check of the laravel: generator now check the keys the transform returns; with a ...data spread, the form fields plus the added keys. A form submitted with a chained form.transform(…).post(…) is found too, also when the chain spans several lines (form / .transform(…) / .post(…)).
  • The Laravel preset picks form components more carefully: a component only gets a role if it has the prop that is bound (an error-state block is no longer used as the field error). A field wrapper component (label + error + slot, e.g. FormField) wraps each field, and textarea and checkbox components are used for text / bool fields; the .callgraph/gen.toml keys are field, textarea and checkbox. The preset also finds form components behind a tsconfig paths / Vite alias (e.g. @ui pointing to a separate UI package), including the ones named in .callgraph/gen.toml, preferring components that existing pages already import.
  • Clearer marks in the output (all languages): reference calls are marked (ref) in the outline, --grep rows and callers. Test functions get [test]; a module of only tests gets [tests] and is collapsed to a count line. Injection, navigation and callback-wiring edges show their kind (inject, nav, wire) in the category column.
  • gen is faster in large PHP projects: unknown type names are resolved with a single project walk (before: one walk per unresolved name), each project file is read at most once per call, and the Laravel preset reads composer.json once.
  • Shorter MCP usage errors: a usage error of generate, rename or undo over MCP no longer appends the whole usage text; the CLI is unchanged. The generate tool description is shorter too — the grammar is in the guide and in the skill's ref/gen.md (MCP: guide with topic: "gen").
  • The laravel: preset writes through the gen generator: FormRequests, controller methods and Inertia/Vue pages now follow the same formatting as gen itself: PHPDoc @return array<string, list<string>|string>, Vue pages with function submit(), long tags wrapped one attribute per line, the @inertiajs/vue3 import first, and const props = only where the script uses it. Ziggy is detected from the composer.json / package.json dependency lists instead of a text search.
  • Stylesheet calls and JSON keys in the outline: CSS/SCSS calls (var(), @include, functions, @extend) appear under their rule and are found by --grep; a var(--brand) call is listed as var(--brand) and is found both as var and as --brand, and functions such as translateY, blur and scale are no longer hidden. A JSON file without methods gets a short key index in the method index (top keys with child counts, runs of scalars collapsed). --format summary counts keys, sections or rules instead of "0 methods" for JSON, Markdown/HTML and stylesheets.
  • More accurate SCSS outline: &--#{$x} and .span-#{$i} keep their full selector name; multi-line selectors and mixin parameter lists are read correctly; @mixin without parentheses and @include x; (a call) work; calls in comments and selector headers are no longer reported; a reassigned $var in the same scope is a write, not a second constant; trailing // comments are recorded. CSS and SCSS now share one engine.
  • Markdown links merged: the outline lists the same link target once, with ×N.
  • No repeated tip over MCP: the closing 💡 tip line is no longer added to every MCP answer (the CLI keeps it). The skill now also recommends callgraph for the structure of md, json, css, scss and html files.
  • Compact Vue outline: props are listed once (a defineProps<X> interface that repeats the component's props is no longer a separate block), emits and models take one line each (emits (N): a, b, …, models (N): name: Type), a prop default longer than the line is cut with …, and component_use paths with a shared folder are written once (dir/{atoms/A, organisms/B}.vue). The outline of a large component is much shorter.
  • A large single-file outline is compacted before the method index: above the output limit, the outline is first shown in a compact form (no comments, constants and properties wrapped, call lists capped at 8 with … +N, every member kept); the method index comes only if even that does not fit. --full shows the whole outline.
  • Grouped callers in the one-line --grep view: when a --grep output is over the limit and falls back to one line per call, each file is a single header line with its callers under it (Cont::caller L12, L40 │ code); a target that is the same for every row is shown once at the top (← target).
  • Shorter --depth output: from level 2, test and story callers collapse into one line (tests/stories: N callers in M files) when there are other callers too, and the whole output is cut at the output limit with a ⚠ line on how to narrow it. --full lists everything.
  • Multi-file --format summary shows the folder: rows of the same folder are grouped under a folder/ header line; a lone file shows its relative path. Above the output limit, a summary shows per-folder totals instead (dir/ N files · C containers · M methods, small folders list their files), so a large project fits in a much shorter answer; --full shows every file.
  • Swift project profile: folders such as Features, Core, Shared, Networking, UI and Persistence get layers; an @Observable / ObservableObject class is a store candidate, View conformers are views, and Codable / Identifiable types are models. More Swift and Foundation built-ins are categorized (pow, defer, math functions, os_log, UIKit and Foundation types).

Fixed

  • Literal import('…') is a use: a dynamic import('./x') or import('pkg') with a fixed string in JS, TS or Vue now links to the file or package, so deps no longer reports such packages as unused and the importing component lists the files it loads.
  • deps: test environment packages are tooling: jsdom, happy-dom, jest-environment-* and @vitest/* are no longer reported as unused.
  • Vue: methods on computed(…).value are not Vue API calls: with const x = computed(…) or ref(…), a call such as x.value.filter(…) is a plain call on the data, no longer reported as a Vue API call.
  • --grep shows the matching line of a chained call: for a call chain spread over several lines, the shown source line is the line of the match, not the first line of the chain.
  • An unknown --option is an error: a mistyped option of an analysis now stops with the usage text instead of printing raw JSONL output.
  • The laravel: preset syntax-checks generated .ts, .js and .html files before writing: before, only PHP and Vue files were checked.
  • Module paths of JS/TS files outside a project: a file with no package.json, tsconfig or jsconfig above it got module paths like home/…; the path is now relative to the file's folder.
  • Rust: the crate's own modules are own code: mod x; and inline mod paths no longer count as a package.
  • --grep <Component>.vue --depth N follows template usage at every level: it was empty from level 2 (also on Windows).
  • Laravel routes in controller groups appear in --format routes: routes inside Route::prefix(…)->name(…)->middleware(…)->controller(X::class)->group(…) (also with an arrow function and nested groups) are listed, and a string action such as 'index' becomes X@index.
  • Laravel routes registered in a loop: a route with an interpolated name (->name("{$code}.x")) makes route('en.x') "dynamic, not verifiable" instead of unknown, and a helper outside routes/ that registers such routes is pointed out. The same applies to groups with a computed prefix or name (Route::prefix($code)->name($code.'.')->group(…), config-driven loops) in --format ziggy.
  • Typed one-line defineEmits is read: defineEmits<{ login: []; save: [id: number] }>() on one line now produces the emits list (--format api).
  • No false calls from template-literal text in Vue attributes: text inside a template literal of a bound attribute (` :title="… név (pl. …)" `) is no longer read as a call (accented letters were the trigger).
  • --format forms no longer drops forms silently: a form submitted to a computed URL (form.post(path.value)) is listed with its route marked unknown/dynamic; a form whose target is a URL or route name missing from the route table (e.g. a package or auth-scaffolding route) is listed with ? not in the route table; and the forms that are still skipped are summed up at the end with the reason and their file and line (? 2 skipped: <reason> (a.vue L3, b.vue L9)). A template string or # inside the useForm({…}) object no longer breaks reading the fields.
  • Optional read-guard hook ignores writes: an output redirect or heredoc is not a read any more, so cat >> f, cat > f <<EOF or 2>f on a large source file is no longer blocked; cat f and cat < f still count.
  • Optional callgraph-first hook accepts a folder as --project: a callgraph run with --project <folder path> (e.g. a git worktree), not only a registered project name, now counts for the files in it, so the hook no longer says that callgraph has not run on that file.
  • --grep useX --depth N skips destructured values: uses of a value destructured from useX() are no longer listed as calls of useX.
  • callgraph.sh rename works: the wrapper script now forwards it (the help already advertised it).
  • The laravel: preset follows the project and the migration: it writes <script setup lang="ts"> with typed props in a TypeScript project even without existing .vue files, and reads the migration column type: text columns get no max:255, string('x', 100) gets max:100.
  • locate caller counts stay within the language family: a Vue function no longer counts the PHP callers of a same-named method.
  • Swift: an Extensions folder is own code: a folder named Extensions with Swift files was treated as vendor.

entry.title: callgraph v1.0.2
entry.content:
Changed

  • The root: line shows the git branch: the root: line at the top of multi-file outputs (and locate) now ends with the branch of the project root, e.g. root: /x/app (branch: feature/z); on a detached HEAD it shows detached <sha7>, and without git it is unchanged. An agent sees at once when it looks at another checkout than the one where the branch was switched (a --project alias pointing to another clone or worktree, an MCP server started in another folder).

Fixed

  • Short ::method selector works in a multi-selector call: callgraph.sh src/Sample.php::alpha ::beta --body now shows both bodies; ::beta reuses the file of the previous selector. Before, it answered "Not found: <root>/". A ::method with no file before it gives a clear usage error, and the help lists the form.

entry.title: callgraph v1.0.1
entry.content:
Fixed

  • Laravel route files loaded from a group keep the group's prefixes: a file loaded with ->group(base_path('routes/admin.php')), ->group(__DIR__.'/admin.php'), a require inside a group, or a group in the then: closure of bootstrap/app.php now inherits the group's URI prefix and route-name prefix. Existing chained names like admin.reports.show are no longer reported as unknown by --format ziggy (false alarms), and rename route checks names the same way.
  • Unnamed routes in a named Laravel group get the group's name: a route without its own ->name() inside a named group now gets the group's combined name, like Laravel does (Route::prefix('x')->name('a')->group(fn () => Route::name('.b')->group(fn () => Route::get('/', ...))) gives a.b), so route('a.b') is no longer reported as unknown by --format ziggy. A route file that is required but left out of the scan (typically a gitignored, local-only file, e.g. if (app()->isLocal()) require __DIR__.'/local.php';) is read from disk and its routes count.

entry.title: callgraph v1.0.0
entry.content:
Added

  • Package recognition (composer, npm, yarn, pnpm, bun): callgraph reads the manifests and lock files (offline) and callgraph.sh profile shows a stack: line with the notable packages and their locked versions (the declared range without a lock, marked); the MCP startup profile gets a compact version of it. profile --packages lists every direct composer / npm dependency (installed and declared version, dev flag).
  • See which package a call goes to, and where a package is used: in the outline, calls into a dependency are grouped under the package's short name (guzzle: GuzzleHttp\Client::request), the JSON output has a package field (versions once per file), and locate gives a "package" reason. callgraph.sh uses <package> [--calls] (MCP package_usage) lists per API symbol how often it is used and the first file; (type) marks an import without a call, --calls lists every call line.
  • callgraph.sh deps (MCP project_profile with deps: true): probably unused, missing and dev-only composer / npm dependencies, one line each with a short reason. A false alarm can be silenced with deps-ignore <name> in .callgraphignore.
  • Inertia pages: a PHP Inertia::render('Board') call links to its page file (Pages/Board.vue), the page's outline gets a rendered by: line, and show . --format inertia lists each page with its render sites and props, marking a missing page file or props the page does not declare in defineProps, plus the pages never rendered.
  • Laravel routes and Ziggy: callgraph reads the route table from the loaded routes/*.php files (groups, resources, names, the /api prefix). A Vue / JS route('events.show') call in the outline shows the method, URI and controller action (or ⚠ no route), and a controller method gets a route: line. show . --format ziggy lists unknown route names and route files that are never loaded; when some routes have dynamic names, unknown names are only marked ?.
  • Laravel form check: an Inertia useForm({...}) form is compared with the validation of the controller action it posts to (FormRequest or inline validate): a form: line under the sending function and under the action (fields sent but not validated, required fields not sent, or N fields ✓); show . --format forms lists them all.
  • Laravel model summary: under an Eloquent model the outline shows table: (the columns from the migrations) and fillable: lines, relation lines show their target, and ⚠ lines warn about a fillable or cast that is not a column. show . --format models lists the models, the tables without a model, and a table created twice without a drop (a fresh migrate would fail).
  • Fast single-file outlines in Laravel projects: the outline of one file reads only the route, migration and form files it needs and keeps the results in .callgraph/laravel.bin (only if .callgraph/ exists; checked against the files' modification time and size, rebuilt automatically, safe to delete). Route files are read in path order, so a controller's route: lines come in the same order in every view.
  • Code generator callgraph.sh gen '<expr>': writes PHP classes / members, Vue single-file components (script setup, template, style), composables, plain JS / TS modules and full HTML pages from a short Emmet-like expression, in the project's style (namespace from composer.json, imports from the project, TS or JS, semicolons, indentation). In a Vue script use:{useX}@/composables/useX is a named import (a bare path becomes one by itself when the file only has export function useX), type:Flag{flag:str,on?:bool} an interface (inline object types such as list<{a:str}> work too), and raw{…} / const:{a,b}=useX() write a statement as is. Targets: --write <file> (new file only), --into <file>[::Class] [--after <method>], --replace <file>:L<a>-L<b> or ::<method>, where --expect <sha256-prefix> refuses the change if those lines changed meanwhile; without a target, or with --dry, it only prints the code. It answers with one line per file. The new text is syntax-checked before writing (nothing is written on an error), every change to an existing file is backed up to .callgraph/backups/ first (newest 10 per file), and callgraph.sh undo [<file>] restores the newest backup.
  • Generator: JS / TS modules and HTML pages: mod:util>fn:join(p:list<str>):str{…}+const:MAX:int=10 writes a module, class:Svc<Base>[Iface]>… a class (members as in PHP: + public, - private, # protected). Everything is exported by default, -fn: keeps a function private, !fn: / !class: makes it export default; a .ts file gets types, a .js file JSDoc. --into x.ts[::Class] adds members, --replace x.ts::fn or x.ts::Class::method replaces one. html:Title[lang=hu]>(head>…)+(body>…) writes a full document (doctype, charset, viewport, title) with the head shortcuts meta:description=…, link:style.css, script:app.js and base:/app/; any element and attribute works, and inline style{…}, script{…} and comment{…} are allowed (CSS and JS checked before writing). --into x.html adds at the end of <body> or into ::#id / ::.class / ::tag, --replace x.html::#id replaces an element.
  • A Laravel feature in one step: gen 'laravel:Fee[auth,prefix=admin]>create(name:str,amount:int,paid?:bool)+edit+index' writes the FormRequests, controller methods, routes and Inertia / Vue pages together, checks that the form fields match the rules, warns about NOT NULL columns without a default that the form does not send, and one undo reverts all of its files.
  • callgraph.sh rename route|class|method <old> <new>: renames across the whole project — route names (->name(), groups, 'profile.*' patterns, resource routes via ->names(), and every route('x') in PHP, Blade, JS and Vue), PHP classes (declaration, file move, namespace, use, type hints, docblocks; --strings also rewrites string references, --keep-table keeps the Eloquent table name) and PHP methods (overrides, resolved calls, callable arrays, route actions). Every changed file is syntax-checked first, --dry only reports, and one undo reverts the whole rename.
  • MCP generate and rename tools (opt-in): listed only when the server runs with --generate or CALLGRAPH_GENERATE=1; without it the tool list stays exactly as before.

Changed

  • MCP tool hints: unlike every other tool, the opt-in generate and rename tools write files, so they declare readOnlyHint: false (and idempotentHint: false); all other tools still declare readOnlyHint: true.
  • Local stats and opt-in telemetry: new command kinds. uses / package_usage, deps, generate, undo and rename are counted as their own commands in the local stats and event log (on this machine, callgraph.sh stats), and — only if you turned telemetry on — in the daily counts that are sent, still without names, paths or code. callgraph.sh telemetry preview shows what would be sent; off: CALLGRAPH_STATS=0 (local), callgraph.sh telemetry off or CALLGRAPH_TELEMETRY=0 (sending).

Fixed

  • PHP: a fully qualified name such as \LogicException or \Helper now resolves to the global namespace, not to the current namespace or an import.
  • An SCSS file with accented characters before a function call (// Fejléc háttér) no longer crashes project-wide views such as locate, profile or the framework views (also in 0.9.5). If a language analyzer crashes on a file, only that file is skipped instead of the whole command failing.

entry.title: callgraph v0.9.5
entry.content:
Added

  • Local command log: callgraph.sh stats --events [--days N] lists your recent calls (command, client, outcome, timing and size bands, how it relates to the previous call, and whether its file / symbol appeared in the previous call's output) and the most common command transitions. A "previous output reused" summary shows per transition how often the next call's file was the first file listed (hit1), the 2nd–5th (hit5), a later one (hit) or not there (miss), and whether its symbol was there (hit / miss). The log stays on this machine (14 days) and contains no names, paths or code; the reuse check keeps only the last call's output items, as keyed hashes in the local session.json, replaced at every call and never sent. Off: CALLGRAPH_STATS=0.

Changed

  • Opt-in telemetry (schema 2): if you turned telemetry on, the daily counts now also include command-order counts (which command followed which, the gap between them, whether the target was the same file, folder or project), session-length bands, the target file's language and size band, and the previous-output bands per command transition (hit1 / hit5 / hit / miss, symbol hit / miss) — still no names, paths, code or hashes. You are told once; callgraph.sh telemetry preview shows exactly what would be sent.
  • The session-start check may suggest sharing usage counts up to 10 times (every 2 days), never after you said no.
  • MCP tools say they only read, and when to use which: every MCP tool now declares readOnlyHint: true, destructiveHint: false, idempotentHint: true and openWorldHint: false, since none of them changes anything or reaches outside the project, so directories that require these hints (e.g. OpenAI's) accept the server. The descriptions of locate, outline, search and framework_view now tell the agent which one fits: outline with method lists what that method calls (so there is no separate callees tool) and points to find_callers for who calls it.

Fixed

  • callgraph.sh telemetry status now lists DO_NOT_TRACK among the reasons sending is blocked.

entry.title: callgraph v0.9.4
entry.content:
Added

  • Session-start check (optional SessionStart hook, callgraph.sh hook install-session; the installer asks): at the start of a new session it tells you when a recommended setting is off (refresh hook, MCP with --auto-update, opting in to shared usage counts) or a newer version is out, and your agent asks you before changing anything. At most every 2 days and 3 times per item; hook never <item>, CALLGRAPH_RECOMMEND=0.

  • MCP Registry: each release now ships callgraph.mcpb (an MCPB bundle with the binaries for all five platforms) and publishes it to the official MCP Registry as io.github.GeRiY/callgraph, so MCPB-aware clients (e.g. Claude Desktop) can install the MCP server in one step, without a Rust toolchain.

Changed

  • Update checks and downloads go through update.callgraph.eu (falls back to GitHub); anonymous daily usage count — see "Anonymous daily count" in the README.

Fixed

  • The release zips now keep the executable bit on the binary and scripts, so a manually unpacked package runs without chmod +x (the installer already set it).

entry.title: callgraph v0.9.3
entry.content:
Added

  • HTML files (.html, .htm): handled as documents like Markdown — the outline lists the <title> and the <h1>–<h6> headings by level with line ranges, --lines works, and --strings searches the visible text and the title / alt / placeholder / aria-label / value attributes (<script>, <style> and comments are skipped). Broken or unclosed HTML does not stop the analysis.
  • locate finds properties and fields: PHP properties (also protected $fillable and promoted constructor properties), TS / JS class fields and parameter properties, Rust struct fields, and Swift / Python / Go properties are definitions (property $fillable L12 ← "fillable" (exact property); fillable, $fillable and Invoice::$fillable all match); part of the name is a name-part match. A property defined in many files (like $fillable in every model) does not push the exact class or a rarer term's files down.

Changed

  • locate ranks names that join several terms first: a definition or file name containing two or more of the searched terms (toggleFavorite for toggle favorite, PodcastEpisodeController for podcast episode) gets a large boost that grows with the number of terms, even when each term alone is too general (the "too general" line stays). Definitions in type declaration files (.d.ts, .pyi) weigh less than real ones and no longer push these files to the top.

Fixed

  • PHP: receivers from the Laravel container are resolved: $x = app(Foo::class), resolve(Foo::class), app()->make(Foo::class), $this->app->make(Foo::class) and App::make(Foo::class) give $x the type Foo (resolved through use and the namespace, like new Foo()), and app(Foo::class)->bar() / resolve(Foo::class)->bar() resolve to Foo::bar, so --grep 'Foo::bar' finds these callers without --guess. A string id (app('foo')) stays unresolved.

entry.title: callgraph v0.9.2
entry.content:
Fixed

  • JS / TS literal computed call target: o['x'](), o["x"]() and o[`x`]() now get the same target as o.x() (the old [] target is gone); o[k]() stays a dynamic_call, a numeric key (a[0]()) no longer yields [].
  • --guess on a single-level --grep: --grep 'Type::method' --guess (and --depth 1 --guess) now also lists the unresolved, name-only callers, marked with ? as in the --depth 2+ view.
  • Single-level --grep 'Type::method' footers: the (+N unresolved, name-only matches skipped — --guess shows them) and (N of these callers contain dynamic calls — check them by hand) lines of the --depth 2+ view now also appear on the single-level view, when there is something to say.

entry.title: callgraph v0.9.1
entry.content:
Added

  • JSX component use is a call: a capitalized JSX element (<Button />, <Button>…</Button>, <Ui.Button />) in .tsx / .jsx / .js is a component_use call (the same category as in Vue), resolved through the import like an ordinary function call, so --grep 'Button$' and --depth find the component's users; a component defined in the same file is an internal_helper. <div> and other lowercase elements, and fragments, are not calls.
  • Vue --format api lists the component's props: (name, type if known, [required]) and emits:.

Fixed

  • JSX in plain .js / .mjs / .cjs files no longer gives syntax error: Unexpected JSX expression and an empty outline: these files are parsed as JSX-capable (as in CRA / babel / vite projects). .ts stays non-JSX (<T>x is a type assertion there).
  • Namespaced --grep pattern (App\Svc\Real::m): a single \ after an identifier character and before a capital letter is read as the namespace separator instead of a regex escape (\S, \R, \B used to match silently wrong or fail); \., \d, \w, \b and a doubled \\ are unchanged. A still-invalid pattern gets a 💡 line explaining the doubling. Same for --depth and callers.
  • --layer / --layers / --by-layer without a path run on the project root (like profile) instead of printing the usage line.
  • The protect 🔒 mark now also shows in --format summary (and the stats header); json, mermaid and dot are unchanged.

entry.title: callgraph v0.9.0
entry.content:
Added

  • dynamic_call marker: calls whose target is decided at runtime used to be missing from the outline, so the graph looked complete where it was not. They are now listed (last, after the other categories) with the called expression as the target — PHP: $obj->$m(), $obj->{$expr}(), $class::$m(), $fn(), new $class, call_user_func($x), app($var) / resolve($var) / $this->app->make($var); JS / TS / Vue: obj[expr](), new (expr)(), import(expr), require(expr); Python: getattr(obj, name)(), globals()[name](), importlib.import_module(name), eval / exec. Literal cases (obj['x'](), app(Foo::class), getattr(obj, 'x')()) stay ordinary. It is a marker, not a caller edge: --grep, --depth and locate ignore it; --depth adds a line telling how many of the callers contain dynamic calls ("check them by hand"). In PHP, callback parameters typed Closure / callable and local closures ($f = fn …) do not count as dynamic calls, and ($this->invokable)() on a class-typed property is a plain Type::__invoke call. Filter with --category dynamic_call. Rust, Swift and Go: not yet.
  • Recovery hints: an empty or wrong result now tells the next step instead of staying silent. --grep with no match explains that the pattern is a regular expression on the call target, suggests the name-only pattern ((^|::|\.|->)name$, --guess) and did you mean: User::find; Not found: <path> and No such method add a second Did you mean: … line (up to 3 similar paths / method names); --depth says whether the target does not exist or exists but nothing calls it; --strings with no match explains the matching rule; locate with no match suggests name parts, English code names and --strings. An unknown --category is now an error listing the known categories (Unknown category: … (known: …)) instead of an empty result. The hints appear in the text output only; json, mermaid, dot, stats and the next suggestions are unchanged.
  • Recipes in the skill: a short "Recipes — task → call sequence" section (bug fix, who calls this, unfamiliar project, where is this text) in the skill instructions, and the same in 3 lines in the MCP instructions.

entry.title: callgraph v0.8.0
entry.content:
Added

  • --help in the binary: callgraph --help, -h and help print the full, current help (English or Hungarian) — the same text as callgraph.sh --help, now also mentioning Python, Go, --signatures, protect and the environment variables.
  • Python (phase 1): .py / .pyi files in the map: classes with bases and decorators, functions, methods (async, @staticmethod, @classmethod, @property), constants, __all__, docstrings, signatures (--signatures, --format api), imports, categorized calls (native_python, internal_helper, static_call, external_call), strings, syntax errors, Django / Flask / FastAPI detection. venv, .venv, site-packages and __pycache__ are skipped by default.
  • Go (phase 1): .go files in the map: structs (fields as properties, embedded types), interfaces, type aliases and defined types, functions and methods with receivers (also when the type is declared in another file), generics, const / var, imports (alias, blank, dot), signatures with several return values (--signatures, --format api), categorized calls (native_go, internal_helper, static_call, instantiation, external_call; go / defer included), strings, doc comments, exported (capitalised) = public, syntax errors, Gin / Echo / Fiber / Chi / gRPC / GORM detection. testdata is skipped by default (vendor already was); _test.go files rank as tests in locate.

entry.title: callgraph v0.7.0
entry.content:
Added

  • protect lines in .callgraphignore: protect migrations/ keeps the matching files in the map (fully queryable) but marks them 🔒 in the outline, --body, --lines, locate and --format json ("protected": true): protected, read them, don't edit them. Same pattern rules as the exclusions; no protect line, no change.
  • Signatures in outlines: --signatures (or CALLGRAPH_SIGNATURES=1) prints the compact signature on the method line of the outline and the --grep caller outlines: updateOrders(array $ids, bool $notify = false): array L4-9 (where the language provides params / return type). --format api now also shows TS / Vue return types, and for PHP a more specific DocBlock type (@return array{updated:int}, list<int>, @param shapes), at most 80 characters.

Changed

  • Non-UTF-8 sources are decoded, not replaced with �: ISO-8859-2, windows-1250 and ISO-8859-1/windows-1252 files are detected and read properly (display, outline, locate, --strings); garbage still falls back to �.
  • Stronger change detection (Linux / macOS): the freshness stamp also includes the inode change time, so a same-size edit with a restored mtime is noticed. The stored graph is rebuilt once, quietly.

entry.title: callgraph v0.6.1
entry.content:
Fixed

  • Files that are not UTF-8 (e.g. ISO-8859-2 / Latin-2) no longer give an empty result: --lines and --body / the MCP method_body printed nothing at all for a file with accented text in another encoding (even in a single comment), with no message. The lines are now printed, with the bytes that are not valid UTF-8 shown as �; the line numbers stay correct.

entry.title: callgraph v0.6.0
entry.content:
Added

  • Suggested next step (opt-in): with CALLGRAPH_NEXT=1 or --next (MCP: callgraph mcp --next), a result can end with one line like ↪ r7 possible next: [1] OrderService.php::refund --body [2] callers of refund [3] outline OrderService.php. The agent runs one by number (callgraph.sh next r7 1, several: next r7 1,3; MCP: the next tool) instead of composing the command. Only read-only navigation, only names that appear in that output, at most 3, and no line at all when nothing is clear (errors, empty results, json / mermaid / dot). Stored in the project's .callgraph/results/ (last 50, 24 hours); callgraph.sh stats shows how often a suggestion was used.
  • Opt-in sending of the usage stats: callgraph.sh telemetry status|preview|on|off. Nothing is sent unless the user turns it on in a terminal (telemetry on asks y/N; an agent cannot do it). Then the closed days' banded counts (the same as stats, no paths or names) go out once a day in the background; CALLGRAPH_TELEMETRY=0 blocks it for good. The installer asks once (Yes / Not now / Never), only in an interactive terminal.
  • Note marker on hits: a 📝 N at the end of the line shows that a hit has notes — in --grep callers (outline, one-line-per-call view, every --depth level; MCP find_callers), in locate file lines and in --format api method lines. Method notes count on the method line; if the method has none, the file's notes. Orphaned notes do not count; without notes the output is unchanged.

Changed

  • stats separates user errors from internal errors: usage mistakes, missing files and unsupported files are counted as "user err" (not logged to errors.jsonl since 0.5.1); "internal" errors are also in errors.jsonl. An unsupported / generated / binary file in callgraph.sh is now a user error (no error-id).
  • One-time notice: the first time local stats are recorded on a machine, one line on stderr says so (and how to turn them off). Never in MCP output.

entry.title: callgraph v0.5.3
entry.content:
Added

  • --strict for CI: a file with a syntax error still gives exit code 0 by default (the partial map is useful). With --strict (or CALLGRAPH_STRICT=1), show (file, folder, --grep), locate and profile exit with code 3 when a file they read has a syntax error; the output is the same.
  • mail and notification layers: Laravel mail classes (extends Mailable, usually in app/Mail) and notifications (extends Notification) get their own layer instead of "unknown". Like event, they need this proof in the code: a folder that is just named Mail is not enough.

Changed

  • The flow: line only shows real call pairs: every A → B in the chain now means A really calls B. A layer that only calls into the middle of the chain is shown as a side branch, e.g. flow: controller → service → model; command → service (before: controller → command → service → model, although controllers never call commands).
  • Enums get no role from their name: app/Enums/PaymentProvider.php was a "provider" just because of its name. An enum (PHP, TS, Rust, Swift) never gets a role from its name now; an Enums folder is shown as enum.
  • Copied framework cores are skipped like vendor code: a framework copied into a legacy project (CodeIgniter system/, Yii framework/, Kohana system/) no longer adds command / handler / request layers to the profile. Only the framework core is skipped, the application code next to it still counts. A big subtree you want left out completely can go into .callgraphignore as a path (sn_monitoring/).

Fixed

  • Syntax errors no longer hide the code after them (JS / TS / Vue, Rust): before, only the functions before the error were mapped; in a Vue <script setup> an error in the first function could leave nothing. Now mapping goes on from the next top-level function, class or item, with the right line numbers; only the broken part is missing.
  • --layer / --layers / --by-layer now agree with the profile: they classified files from folder names only, so app/Actions/Event/*Action.php showed up as [event] although the profile did not list an event layer. They now use the same rules and code proof as profile (from the project map; without it, a folder like Event gives the next role, e.g. service). Files skipped as vendor or build output get no layer here either.
  • callgraph.sh --project <dir>: a folder path (absolute or relative) now works with every command, without registering it; before, file queries said "No projects.json — register a project first". An unknown alias still gives an error.

entry.title: callgraph v0.5.2
entry.content:
Added

  • update --dev: installs the newest build of the develop branch (version X.Y.Z-dev.<commit>, checked against its SHA256SUMS like a release); update --check --dev only tells you whether there is a newer one. A plain update takes you back to the latest stable release. The daily background check and the MCP --auto-update stay on stable releases. On a dev build callgraph --version shows the dev version.

Changed

  • The changelog in Hungarian too: CHANGELOG.hu.md has every release in Hungarian, and the Hungarian website shows it.

Fixed

  • update --check right after a release: for a few minutes after a new release it could still say "up to date", because GitHub briefly served the old answer. It now asks without the cache and also looks at the list of recent releases, so a new version is found immediately.

entry.title: callgraph v0.5.1
entry.content:
Added

  • Local usage stats: callgraph.sh stats shows how you (and your agents) used callgraph in the last 7 days (--days N for up to 90): how many calls per command and MCP tool, how many failed, how long they took and how big the output was, and for locate how often the first result was the file the agent opened next. Everything stays on your computer: nothing is sent anywhere, and no paths, names or search terms are recorded — only counts in ranges. The data is in the skill folder (stats/, about 90 days); turn it off with CALLGRAPH_STATS=0.
  • --no-gitignore: add it to any command (show, folder views, locate, profile, refresh, callers) to also map the files your .gitignore excludes; for the MCP server and the hook set CALLGRAPH_GITIGNORE=0. .callgraphignore and the always-skipped folders (vendor, node_modules, …) still apply.
  • locate route::events.show: finds a route by its name: the definition (->name('events.show') in routes/*.php) comes first, then every route('events.show'), to_route(…) and redirect()->route(…) in PHP and JavaScript / TypeScript / Vue. If nothing is found, it says what it looked for.
  • callgraph.sh --version (also -V and version) prints the version, the platform and where the binary is.

Changed

  • .callgraphignore accepts paths: a line like md, .md or *.md still skips an extension, and every other line is now a path pattern written like in .gitignore (public/build/, /storage/, !keep.js), relative to the folder of the file. A bare word such as build is still an extension; write build/ for a folder.
  • locate ranks exact matches first: a file whose class, component or function name (or file name) is one of the terms now always comes before files that only contain the terms as text, such as translation files or build output.
  • A quoted phrase is one locate term: locate "Organizer's other events" searches for the whole text in the strings of the code (labels, translations) instead of splitting it into words that matched unrelated names.
  • locate always shows a root: line and paths relative to it, also when only one file matches.
  • The profile lists the main layers first: the architecture layers (controller, service, model …) come first, by file count, and tests, migrations and configuration come last, so a main layer such as model no longer hides behind … +6 more layers while layers with one or two files are shown.
  • --by-layer shows a header for each layer: every group of callers starts with a line such as [service] 3 calls, in the normal and in the short ("one line per call") --grep view, and in every level of --depth. The group closest to the called method comes first (model → repository → service → controller), as the help says; before, only a [service] tag at the end of some lines showed the layer.
  • User mistakes are no longer logged as tool errors: a mistyped layer name, an unknown option or a file that does not exist now prints just the message — no [error-id: …] line, no bug-report link, and nothing is written to errors.jsonl. Real internal errors are still logged and get an error-id.
  • JSON outlines show the values: scripts.build = "vite build" and devDependencies.vite = "^6.0" instead of just string; numbers, true / false and null as they are, strings over 60 characters cut with …, and objects and lists with their size (object (3), array (2)).
  • Read one JSON key: callgraph.sh package.json::scripts --body prints that key with its exact lines; use dots for deeper keys (scripts.build) and numbers for list items (files.0). Before, it said "No such method".
  • locate finds JSON keys: locate laravel-vite-plugin now lists package.json with the line of the key. Only the exact key name (or the whole dotted path) counts, so searches for other words do not fill up with JSON files.
  • CSS and SCSS rules are no longer written like functions: .p-toast L29-31 instead of .p-toast(); mixins and functions keep their ().

Fixed

  • CSS outlines list every rule: some rules were missing (a rule with the selector .p-toast was always left out, and so was the first rule after @charset), and at-rules were not shown at all. Now every rule and at-rule is listed with its lines: @import, @tailwind, @media, @supports, @layer, @keyframes, @font-face, and the Tailwind v4 @theme, @utility, @custom-variant, @variant, @plugin, @source and @config.
  • CSS rules start on the right line: a rule after a comment or another rule showed the line where the previous rule ended (.p-datepicker-panel L31-41 instead of L39-41).
  • CSS paths with /* inside quotes stay whole: @source '../**/*.blade.php' was cut, because the /* in the path was taken for the start of a comment.
  • PHP and JavaScript layers are no longer mixed up in the profile: in a project with PHP controllers and AngularJS (or other JavaScript) controllers, the profile showed one controller layer with all of them. A role that exists in more than one language is now shown apart, e.g. controller (php) and controller (js), and the call direction (flow:) no longer joins the backend and the frontend through a shared name such as service. Projects with one language look exactly as before. --layer controller still finds both; --layer controller:js (or --layer "controller (js)") only the JavaScript ones.
  • Third-party code no longer makes up the project's architecture: an SDK or library copied into the project (a subfolder with its own composer.json, package.json or LICENSE, or folders such as vendors/, third_party/, extensions/, external/, libs/) gave the profile layers and patterns (Builder, Factory, Handler…) that the project itself does not have. These files are now left out of the profile, and one line says so, e.g. vendor: 312 files skipped (extensions/Facebook, vendors/phpoffice, …). Searches and folder views still see them. profile --with-vendor counts them again.
  • Copies of build output are left out of the profile: folders named dist, build or *.min (such as web/assets.min) and minified files no longer count twice as layers; a generated: N files skipped (…) line shows them.
  • A folder named after a business topic is not an event layer: app/Services/Event or a JavaScript controllers/event folder became an event layer. event, listener and job now need proof in the code — an Event / Listener / Subscriber base class or interface, Laravel's Dispatchable or ShouldQueue, or a handle(…) method in a Listeners namespace; otherwise the file keeps its other role (service, controller, model for app/Models/Job.php).
  • Files your .gitignore excludes no longer show up: the build output of a Laravel + Vite project (public/build/assets/app-CBW7lKWe.js, listed in .gitignore as /public/build) appeared in locate and folder views. .gitignore now works the way git reads it: patterns with a leading /, nested paths, **, ! exceptions and a .gitignore in any subfolder. The same rules apply everywhere callgraph looks at files, including the MCP server's file watcher and the editor hook.
  • Minified and bundled JavaScript / CSS is skipped even without a .min. name or a .gitignore: a file whose first lines are extremely long is recognised as generated and left out.
  • locate --orange-500 (a CSS variable) was rejected as an unknown option; it is now searched for. The known options (--all, --project) still work as before.
  • callgraph.sh --version printed the usage of show and logged an error.
  • Files with a syntax error are no longer shown as if they were complete: a file you are in the middle of editing, or one with a merge conflict, could come back with no functions at all (JavaScript, TypeScript, Vue, Rust) or without any notice (PHP, Swift). A search then said "no such method" or found no callers, which could make an agent think the code was unused. Now the parts before the error are kept (functions a and b stay visible when c is broken), and every result says so: ⚠ syntax error at L3: … — this file's outline may be incomplete under the file, a closing line such as ⚠ 2 files had syntax errors (results may be incomplete): src/tail.js L3, src/v.vue L4 when a folder, a search (--grep, --depth), locate or profile read a broken file, parseErrors in --format json, and a warning on the error output of callers. The exit code stays 0, because the rest of the result is still correct and useful. Covers JavaScript, TypeScript, Vue, PHP, Rust, Swift and JSON (CSS, SCSS and Markdown are read leniently and are not flagged).

entry.title: callgraph v0.5.0
entry.content:
Added

  • Where to start with a task — locate: give it the names and terms from a task in one go (callgraph.sh locate RefundController processRefund refund payment_status checkout.vue, or the new locate tool over MCP) and it lists the few files worth opening first, best first, each with the reason: the class or method of that name, the file of that name, a name that contains the word (refund → RefundJob, refunds_table), a text such as a column name or route, or a call to it. It answers from the project map without reading the code again, so it is quick. A file that matches several of your terms comes before one that matches a single term many times. It shows 5 files (--all for every match) and says which terms found nothing and which are too general. The skill and MCP instructions now also tell agents when to use it, and when plain text search (grep) is the better tool.
  • Project profile: callgraph.sh profile tells you in about 15 lines how an unfamiliar project is built: the architecture (Laravel / Yii layered MVC, DDD / hexagonal, Vue / React frontend, SwiftUI MVVM, Rust web), which folder holds which layer (controllers, services, repositories, models, components, stores…) with file counts, the design patterns it uses (Repository, Factory, Strategy, Observer…), the folders with no clear role, and whether the layers call each other in the expected direction. It reads folder and file names and checks them against the code graph (extends Controller, implements *RepositoryInterface, defineStore); what it cannot tell stays "unknown". --full shows every folder. For AI clients: the project_profile MCP tool, and a short profile is sent when a client connects.
  • Layers in queries (opt-in, nothing changes by default): --layer service searches only the files of that layer (no need to know the folder names), --layers groups the summary by layer and marks each file with its role, --by-layer orders "who calls it?" results by layer, closest to the called code first (also for callers, and as layer / by_layer on the MCP tools). Folder names that say nothing, or are not English, can be mapped in a commit-able .callgraph-layers file (service = app/Logic, ignore-role = app/Legacy).
  • Exclude extensions per project: a .callgraphignore file in the project root (or in any subfolder; the nearest one applies) lists extensions callgraph should skip there, one per line (md, .json or *.vue; # starts a comment). Commit it, and everyone on the team gets the same results. A file you name directly with an excluded extension is refused with a clear message.

Changed

  • Only supported files are processed, more strictly: callgraph already ignored files with other extensions; now it also skips generated files (package-lock.json, *.min.js, *.min.css) and files with binary content, even when their extension is supported. Naming one of them directly gives a clear reason instead of a result.
  • Upper-case extensions count: B.PHP, App.TS or Main.Vue are now processed like their lower-case versions (before, they were silently skipped).

Fixed

  • A file reached through a symlink is no longer listed twice: if a symlink pointed to a file inside the project, that file appeared (and was analysed) twice in folder results.
  • Windows: the short summary shows file names again: when a folder's output was too long and callgraph showed the one-line-per-file summary instead, Windows listed each file with its full path instead of just its name.

entry.title: callgraph v0.4.0
entry.content:
Added

  • Refresh the project map ahead of time: callgraph.sh refresh brings the project map in .callgraph/ up to date right away — every changed, new or deleted file, or only the files / folders you name — and prints a one-line summary. Handy after a git pull or after an agent wrote many files: the next query no longer has to re-analyse them. --background returns at once and does the work in a separate process. Two refreshes never work on the same project at the same time; if one is already running, the other simply skips.
  • Optional Claude Code hook: after Claude edits or writes a file, callgraph refreshes that file in the background, so the next question about it is answered instantly. The installer asks whether to add it (install.sh --hooks adds it without asking); it only adds one entry to ~/.claude/settings.json, keeps all other settings and hooks, and saves a settings.json.bak backup first. Check or remove it any time: callgraph.sh hook status / callgraph.sh hook uninstall. It does nothing outside registered projects (or ones that already have a .callgraph/ folder).
  • The MCP server keeps itself up to date: while callgraph mcp runs, it watches the projects it has opened and refreshes changed files a moment after they are saved, so queries stay fast. The answers are exactly the same as before. If watching is not possible on a system, it says so once and works as before. To switch it off, set CALLGRAPH_WATCH=0.
  • The MCP server explains itself: AI tools that use callgraph through MCP (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code) now get a short usage guide when they connect, in your language: which tool to use when, how to find every caller of a function, and how to read the answers. A new guide tool gives them the full manual on request. The tool descriptions now each carry an example and the most common mistake to avoid. The guide is made from the same text as the skill's SKILL.md, so the two always say the same thing.
  • The installer can set up the MCP server for Claude Code: if the claude command is available, install.sh asks whether to register callgraph as an MCP server (install.sh --mcp does it without asking, --no-mcp skips it). Running it again does not create duplicates. It prints how to remove it (claude mcp remove -s user callgraph) and where to find the setup for Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code. If this step fails, the rest of the install still completes. The installer now ends with a reminder to restart Claude Code.
  • The MCP server can update itself: add --auto-update to the server's arguments in your AI tool's MCP settings ("args": ["mcp", "--auto-update"], recommended). When the tool starts the server — at most once a day — it checks for a newer callgraph release, downloads it, checks that the file is exactly the published one (it never installs a file whose checksum does not match), installs it just like callgraph.sh update (your projects and settings are kept) and restarts itself, so the tool works with the new version right away. If anything goes wrong (no internet, GitHub limit, a bad download, no write permission) it simply starts the version you have and writes one line to the tool's log. It only writes into callgraph's own folder, never into your projects.
  • The MCP server tells you about updates: without --auto-update, the server checks for a newer release at most once a day in the background (it never makes a request wait) and adds one line to the first answer of the session: ℹ callgraph X is available (installed: Y) — update: …/callgraph.sh update, or add --auto-update to the MCP config. CALLGRAPH_UPDATE_CHECK=0 turns off all update checks (no network at all); they are also off in CI.

Changed

  • Comments inside a method stay in --body: the short method view used to hide comment lines inside the method too, so an agent could think a line was missing and read the file again. Now only the docblock above the method and blank lines are left out; comments inside the method (they often explain the intent) are shown. When a docblock was left out, the header line says so, e.g. (docblock L112-119 omitted: --doc). --doc still adds the docblock, --raw still prints the exact source. The MCP method_body tool works the same way.
  • The project website has its own domain: https://callgraph.eu (the old geriy.github.io/callgraph address redirects).

Fixed

  • "Who calls it" now finds calls from child classes: searching for a method with its class name (--grep FrontendController::redirectToNewDashboard, or the MCP find_callers tool) missed the places where a child class calls the inherited method as $this->redirectToNewDashboard() — only the bare method name found them. Now these calls are found too, marked with the child class (L139 via EventeditController │ …). A child class that has its own version of the method is not counted, because its call runs its own version.

entry.title: callgraph v0.3.0
entry.content:
Changed

  • Faster queries on big projects: callgraph now keeps a compact project map in .callgraph/ in just three files, however big the project is: a short list of all files, one file with every file's full analysis, and one with the summary that searches need. It is updated file by file, only for files that changed since the last query (deleted or renamed files drop out). "Where is it called" (--grep, every --depth level), callers, --strings and --const are answered from the summary file in one read; a single-file view (outline, --body …) reads just that file's part of the full-analysis file. The output is exactly the same as before. An edited file shows up in the very next query; anything damaged or written by another callgraph version is rebuilt quietly. The map replaces the old analysis cache (cache.jsonl), which is removed automatically, so the folder takes less space than before. The MCP server (callgraph mcp) keeps the map in memory between requests. To switch it off (e.g. to compare), set CALLGRAPH_NO_GRAPH=1. Details: docs/PROJECT-GRAPH.md.
  • Shorter call lists in "where is it called" results: when one caller method makes the same call on several lines with the very same source text, it is now shown once with all its line numbers, e.g. L12, L40 │ $this->repo->find($id). Each caller shows at most 3 such rows; the rest are listed by line number only: … +2 more: L55, L61. This applies to --grep, the first --depth level and the one-line-per-call view used when the result would be too long. Calls through an interface stay on their own row (via …).
  • Shorter method bodies: --body now leaves out what an agent rarely needs: the docblock / doc comments above the method, blank lines and lines that are only a comment. Code lines are printed exactly as written (a comment at the end of a code line stays), and nothing inside a string, heredoc or template literal is ever removed. The line numbers are still the real ones, so a gap shows where lines were skipped and you can still read an exact range. Attributes such as #[test] / #[Route(...)] are kept. Works for PHP, JS / TS / Vue, Rust and Swift, for several methods at once and for --grep … --body.
  • New --doc adds the docblock back; new --raw prints the exact, unfiltered source (as before, plus Rust / Swift doc comments and attributes). The MCP method_body tool follows the same default and has doc / raw options.

Added

  • Notes on files and methods (pilot): callgraph note add <file>[::<method>] "<text>" (also callgraph.sh note …) attaches a short note, stored outside the source in <project>/.callgraph/notes.jsonl (git-ignored) with the date and time (UTC). The outline shows it under the file header or the method (📝 2026-11-05 20:27 · text, newest first, at most 3), --body above the method source. note list [<path>] lists them (with [orphaned] when the method is gone), note rm <id> deletes one, and show <dir> --notes <pattern> searches them. The anchor is the method name, not a line number. MCP: a new read-only notes tool (there is no write tool). Without notes the output is unchanged. Details: docs/NOTES.md.
  • TypeScript: calls through typed objects and interfaces. callgraph now works out which class a TS method call goes to when the type is written down: a typed parameter (repo: Repo), a typed class property (private repo: Repo, also constructor(private repo: Repo)), this.repo = new Repo() or const x = new Repo(). So this.repo.find() shows up as Repo::find, and --grep 'Repo::find' finds it. Classes record their implements, and TS interfaces (interface X extends Y) appear in the map, so searching PlaylistResolver::getPlayables also finds calls made through its Resolver interface, marked via Resolver (in --depth and callers too). When the type is unclear (no type, any, a union like Repo | null, a generic T, or different values in the same function) the call stays as before.
  • --const lists re-exports: besides references and definitions, --const NAME now shows where a name is passed on, marked [re-export]: Rust pub use state::{CheckState, STATE_FILE}; / pub(crate) use …, JS / TS export { NAME } from './x' / export { NAME }, PHP use const App\NAME;.

Fixed

  • --grep <pattern> --body prints the source of the caller methods again (the option was ignored).
  • MCP method_body: method may be a single name as a plain string as well as a list (some clients send "method": "parse", which used to fail with an "expected a sequence" error).

Fixed

  • JS/TS: no more doubled methods when a class is named like its file (PlaylistResolver.ts with class PlaylistResolver): the class's methods were listed twice, once under the file's module entry and once under the class. Now class members appear only under the class and top-level functions only under the module.

entry.title: callgraph v0.2.0
entry.content:
Added

  • Background update check: at most once a day callgraph.sh checks GitHub in a detached background process (never slows a query down). If a newer release exists, the output ends with one line, once a day: ℹ callgraph X is available (installed: Y) — update: bash …/callgraph.sh update. Claude Code tells the user and offers the update; it never updates on its own. Opt out with CALLGRAPH_UPDATE_CHECK=0; off in CI.
